item.title: Guide: GTA 6 Release Times: When Can You Start Playing?
item.summary: All the GTA 6 release info you need. Probably the most anticipated game of all time, GTA 6 is now just hours away! We're in the final home stretch now, with availability rolling out on PS5 worldwide within the next 24 hours. As the launch draws even closer, we're covering absolutely everything you need to know about its PS5 launch, including preload options and release times. In this GTA 6 guide , we cover the GTA 6 release times . Read the full article on pushsquare.com
item.text:
Probably the most anticipated game of all time, GTA 6 is now just hours away! We're in the final home stretch now, with availability rolling out on PS5 worldwide within the next 24 hours.
As the launch draws even closer, we're covering absolutely everything you need to know about its PS5 launch, including preload options and release times. In this GTA 6 guide, we cover the GTA 6 release times.
Rockstar has confirmed GTA 6 will officially be playable from midnight on 19th November in your local time zone. If you have preloaded the game, it'll unlock at midnight, and then you can begin playing immediately.
As such, the game will unlock and be available first in New Zealand. Availability will then roll out worldwide as each time zone reaches midnight on 19th November.
When the game launches in the UK, we'll have a hub live on the home page documenting our coverage and providing a place for you to share your first experiences with GTA 6.
GTA 6 preload is available now! If you've pre-ordered from the PS Store, your download of the game should have started and will then be ready for you to start playing at release.
Rockstar has now officially confirmed the GTA 6 file size on PS5, and what you'll need to download, is 212GB. This is one of the biggest downloads and installs on console in history, and will probably only get bigger through patches and the addition of GTA Online.
Can You Play GTA 6 Early with a New Zealand Account?
GTA 6 will unlock and be playable in New Zealand first, as it's located in one of the furthest along timezones. The chances are New Zealand is further along in the day compared to wherever you live in the world, so yes, New Zealand will be the first to gain access to GTA 6.
Because of this, there's been a rising trend in people creating New Zealand PSN account to play games as soon as possible. This can be done with GTA 6 too, but you'll need to set up a fresh New Zealand PSN account and buy the game through its PS Store.
When you have done, you'll be able to play GTA 6 a few hours ahead of other countries like the USA. Keep in mind, though, that you can't transfer your save data from the New Zealand account you set up to your normal profile.
What's the GTA 6 New Zealand Release Time?
If you were to play GTA 6 early via the New Zealand method detailed above, you get access to the game at these times:North America: 3am PST / 4am MST / 5am CST / 6am ESTUK/Ire: 11am GMTEurope: 12pm CET / 1pm EETAsia/Oceania: 8pm JST / 7pm AWST / 10pm AEDT
GTA 6 is available digitally on the PS Store, or in a basic physical version that ships without a disc. The latter provides a code in the box that you redeem on the PS Store to get the digital version.
The two PS5 digital versions on offer are: Standard Edition and Ultimate Edition.

verdict.post:
🎮 GTA 6: старт через пару часов

Rockstar подтвердила: игра станет доступна с полуночи 19 ноября по местному времени. Первыми загрузят новозеландцы, дальше волна пойдёт по часам. Файл на PS5 весит 212 ГБ, так что если не догрузили — бежите к роутеру.

item.title: How Grand Theft Auto 6 Can Be Nominated At The Game Awards Despite Not Being Out Yet
item.summary: Rockstar’s open-world crime drama scored multiple nominations, including Game of the Year
item.text:
The Game Awards just announced its 2026 nominees, and while some of the names that got repeat nods are likely not a surprise to anyone, one of them might be. Grand Theft Auto 6, a game that’s not even out yet, is the most-nominated game of the show this year. As of this writing, reviews haven’t even been published. So, in a roundabout way, some have suggested the early nominations have “spoiled” the reviews and the forthcoming reception to the game.
For those who don’t know how the Game Awards work, the nominees and winners are submitted and voted upon by a jury of media outlets (Kotaku doesn’t participate). Outlets submit ballots, the games that get the most votes are made into nominees, and the media jury then casts votes for the winners. These votes make up 90 percent of the final result. The other 10 percent is determined by a fan vote on the official Game Awards website that begins after the nominations are announced.
This year’s Game Awards cutoff allowed for all games released before November 20 to be nominated, which means that Grand Theft Auto 6, out November 19, barely slid into the eligibility window. But the nomination has still confused a lot of people because host Geoff Keighley didn’t explain the logistics of the nominating process during today’s announcement stream. It’s a rare circumstance for a game to be nominated but not officially out.
But the existence of an explanation hasn’t stopped some folks from crying foul, calling the show “rigged,” and claiming that no one has played this game yet. Some also argue that it doesn’t make sense for the player voting to be open when the game hasn’t yet been made available to the public. Maybe the Game Awards should have held off on doing the whole nominations announcement until the weekend?
Funnily enough, the Game Awards also confirmed something about GTA 6 that Rockstar Games hasn’t publicly confirmed yet. It revealed that Manny L. Perez is playing Lucia, one of the game’s protagonists. She was nominated in the Best Performance category, but hasn’t been able to publicly confirm that she’s in the game.

item.title: GTA 6's Release Will Stress The Internet Just As Everything's Falling Apart
item.summary: GTA 6 is releasing within days of major outages for Apple, Microsoft, and Chase Bank
item.text:
In early November, some internet service providers warned their customers that pre-downloads of Grand Theft Auto 6 were causing network slowdown issues for everyone on the service. That problem became visible before millions of gamers tried to log into the same game simultaneously. A long list of recent outages and issues across industries reliant on tech and network services now makes it seem likely that the biggest game launch of all time won't go down smoothly.
If you've ever been around for the release of a big new game, you know that day-one network issues are fairly common. Some hiccups are worse than others, of course, but most people are probably already bracing for some potential hitches when we're talking about the biggest game launch of all time. What makes GTA 6 different from other game releases is its scale and timing.
The highly anticipated sequel first began causing issues for some ISPs when Rockstar opened preloads for the 212 GB game on Nov. 10. At the time, some providers claimed that the game was directly responsible for never-before-seen traffic peaks so high that they congested the proverbial internet tubes for everyone else.
Rockstar undoubtedly foresaw that the problem could occur or worsen by launch day. The studio dropped a couple of patches in a staggered rollout prior to launch. The release cadence made it less likely that GTA 6 fans could overload Rockstar's, PlayStation's, and Xbox's servers at the same time. Service providers have also been gearing up for Nov. 19, with at least one ISP advertising that it would offer increased download speeds specifically for GTA 6.
Yet network issues of some sort, both in the game and the internet at large, may be unavoidable on Thursday. Recent trends show that many online services are already hanging on by a thread. Earlier in November, flights across the country were halted due to apparent issues with aging routers that could not handle the amount of data shared by newer pieces of equipment. During that same week, Microsoft products like Outlook and Excel went dark for nearly 24 hours because a faulty gateway was overwhelmed by the amount of data passing through it. On Nov. 16, customers were unable to access accounts at major banks like Chase or through payment services like Zelle.
On Nov. 17, Apple users reported widespread issues with iCloud, AppleCare, App Store, and Apple Music. Apple has not revealed the cause of the issues, noting only that outages are slowing down services. On that same Tuesday, news broke that the United States' national security network also went down after weeks of wonkiness.
The quick succession of these instances has led to conspiracy theories online that they're the result of cyberattacks. So far, there's no evidence to support such suspicions in relation to recent newsworthy outages. It's probable that the specific causes of all of these events vary widely, but there's an overarching theme among all of them. Online services, by and large, are built on fragile interconnected systems. Some of those systems rely on old hardware and software that are buckling under normal but increasing strain. Even modernizing systems are not immune — those efforts may actually be responsible for the sudden tech difficulties.
Kris Beevers, CEO of a network and infrastructure company, told the BBC on Monday, “I expect we’ll see more meaningful outages in the infrastructure that essential parts of society depend on in coming months as the invisible infrastructure that our world depends on becomes more strained and visible.”
Since GTA 6 is already responsible for an internet-wide slowdown by some ISPs, it may not be a bad idea to preload the game and its updates ASAP. The same advice applies to those who have purchased physical copies — the game has to be downloaded from Rockstar. Nov. 19 will still probably be rocky for the game if not for the entire internet. But hey: if GTA 6 took over a decade to get here, what's another day?

verdict.post:
📡 GTA 6 уже ломает интернет

Прелоад игры весом 212 ГБ вызвал пиковые нагрузки на сети провайдеров ещё до релиза. Совпадение с недавними сбоями в Apple, Microsoft и банках намекает, что 19 ноября онлайн-сервисы могут зависнуть насовсем. Совет: качайте игру заранее, пока труба не лопнула.
verdict.reason: Актуальная техническая новость о влиянии релиза на инфраструктуру, подтвержденная данными провайдеров и новостным фоном.

item.title: New Zealand Is Bragging That It Gets to Play GTA 6 First
item.summary: New Zealand's official tourism agency posted a playful video celebrating the country's time zone advantage for playing GTA 6 first.
item.text:
Countries do not usually compete over who boots up a video game first. Even getting a rating can be contentious for Grand Theft Auto. New Zealand is not most countries. Its official government tourism agency has posted about the one race the islands win by geography alone, being first to midnight, which this week means first in the world to play Grand Theft Auto VI from Rockstar Games.
The bragging rights are real and officially sanctioned. Rockstar and Sony adopted a rolling midnight launch by country and the first in line is New Zealand at 12:00 AM NZDT on November 19, hours before anyone in Europe or the Americas can touch it. We broke down exactly when the game unlocks in every region and New Zealand sits at the very front of that line every single time.
The government apparently noticed. As reporter Gene Park flagged, New Zealand's tourism account jumped on the "we get it first" conversation with a playful video, turning a quirk of the international date line into a tourism beat.
A national tourism board using a game about crime in a parody of America to flex its time zone is the kind of thing only a launch this size could produce. Every other country spent the week fighting over days off work and clearing 212GB of storage. New Zealand just has to wait for its own clock, which ticks over before everyone else's.
It is one more sign of the gravity we have watched this launch build since marketing ramped up, as promised, the kind that has businesses closing for the day, Sensor Tower projecting a hit to Fortnite's player count and a steady countdown the whole world is watching.
When a government tourism agency works your release date into its pitch, the game has become a global event with a start time.
For once, sitting at the edge of the map is the ultimate cheat code. While the rest of us refresh our consoles and watch the clock, New Zealand will already be driving through Vice City and its government would very much like you to know it.
